exposure: early intravenous ceftriaxone 30-60 minutes prior to skin incision
late intravenous ceftriaxone immediately following cord clamping
outcome: surgical site infections (superficial SSI, deep incisional SSI)
cohort: The study included 150 women scheduled for elective caesarean sections.
finding: The administration of ceftriaxone prior to skin incision resulted in a significant reduction in pyrexia compared to administration after cord clamping, with a modest overall reduction in infection morbidity following cesarean section.
